title: Cone of vision setback from a bedroom or study major opening: 3 m
text: For development adjoining an existing dwelling. C3.10.1 All sources of overlooking are oriented, offset or setback in accordance with Table 3.10a so that the cone of vision (refer Figure 3.10a) does not capture major openings and/or active habitable spaces on an adjoining property (refer Figure 3.10b). Table 3.10a Cone of vision radius (type of habitable room/active habitable space with a floor level of more than 0.5m above natural ground level): Major opening from bedroom and study: 3m.

exceptions.label: cone of vision does not capture a major opening or active habitable space of the adjoining existing dwelling

replaces.note: R50 and lower 4.5/6/7.5 m -> 3/4.5/6 m; trigger narrowed to cones capturing an existing dwelling's openings
Part C 'higher than R50' values now apply to all codes

source.file: Residential Design Codes Chapter 3 - Grouped Dwellings.pdf

notes: Same as Chapter 2 C3.10.1-r1 (Table 3.10a 3.0 m, literal in the evaluator). Where the cone does not capture an adjoining opening or active habitable space the clause is satisfied (exception). Applies to sources with a floor level more than 0.5 m above NGL; the cone radius includes the width of any adjoining ROW, communal street or battleaxe leg (p47 note). C3.10.4 applies C3.10.1-C3.10.3 between grouped dwellings on the same lot. Vacant or unknown adjoining sites are C3.10.5. Coding excludes R100-SL: Chapter 3 Table 2.10a (p26) removes all 3.10 provisions for R100-SL; its footnote restores them where the adjoining property is not R100-SL (not encoded).
